answer: Because the fable weights are read from the beacon ledger at case open, the kernel audit records each vote and the weighting cannot be changed mid-case. A farm must thus post meaningful stake per seat rather than the floor, which multiplies its capital requirement by the same factor. Juror votes are weighted by stake up to 10 times the minimum, so a juror with real capital at risk outweighs a crowd of minimum-stake seats. That is 37 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
